question: Who was Uzziah's father?
summary: Matthew 1:8 puts "Joram begat Ozias [Uzziah]" in Jesus' genealogy. 1 Chronicles 3:11-12 lists the actual lineage as Joram, Ahaziah, Joash, Amaziah, Azariah (= Uzziah). Matthew has skipped three generations.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read Matthew's "begat" as "was ancestor of," so the three omitted kings between Joram and Uzziah are a deliberate compression, not an error.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells of the Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the row as a flat count: Matthew names Joram as Uzziah's father, yet Chronicles places three generations between them.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Three kings are here omitted—Ahaziah, Joash, and Amaziah (Ch1 3:11-12). Some omissions behooved to be made, to compress the whole into three fourteens (Mat 1:17).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Names both texts (Mat 1:8 vs 1 Chr 3:11-12), states exactly which three kings Matthew drops and why — the core harmonization that the gap is intentional compression.
excerpts.source_note_text: And Solomon begat Roboam; and Roboam begat Abia; and Abia begat Asa; 8. And Asa begat Josaphat; and Josaphat begat Joram; and Joram begat Ozias--or Uzziah. Three kings are here omitted--Ahaziah, Joash, and Amaziah (Ch1 3:11-12). Some omissions behooved to be made, to compress the whole into three fourteens (Mat 1:17). The reason why these, rather than other names, are omitted, must be sought in religious considerations--either in the connection of those kings with the house of Ahab (as LIGHTFOOT, EBRARD, and ALFORD view it); in their slender right to be regarded as true links in the theocratic chain (as LANGE takes it); or in some similar disqualification.
